cli.usage:
brain-kit {version}

Usage: brain-kit <command> [options]

Commands available in this version:
  hook <stop|session-start>                                              entry point for the Claude Code plugin hooks (reads the event JSON from stdin)
  validate [dir] [--only-problems] [--json]                              check a vault against the Open Knowledge Format and this vault's own house rules
  lint [dir] [--rule <id>...] [--base auto|worktree|merge-base|all] [--json]   check a vault's own health rules (orphans, tables, secrets, and more)
  --version                                                              print the version
  --help                                                                 print this help

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failure, 2 usage or not inside a vault, 3 degraded, 4 required source not read, 69 network or connector unavailable, 75 postponed (retry later).
validate.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit validate: "{dir}" is not a directory.
validate.no_vault: brain-kit validate: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and {index}).
validate.explain_must: These findings mean the bundle is not conformant to the Open Knowledge Format.
validate.explain_should: These findings mean the vault departs from the format's own guidance, without breaking conformance.
validate.explain_house: These findings mean the vault departs from its own house rules: what its configuration declares, plus the defaults it left in place. The format defines no conformance tier for them.
validate.explain_defect: These findings carry a ruler and level this command does not recognize. This is a defect in brain-kit itself, not in your vault; please report it.
validate.explain_stale: This is informational only and never affects the exit code.
validate.stale_none: No note has passed its stale_after date.
validate.verdict_clean: Result: no findings. The vault is conformant and has no departures.
validate.verdict_clean_with_stale: Result: no conformance or house findings. The vault is conformant; the stale notes listed above are informational only and do not change this.
validate.verdict_warnings_only: Result: the vault is conformant. Every finding above was downgraded to a warning; nothing blocks this run.
validate.verdict_not_blocking: Result: the findings above do not fail this run, because this vault sets validate.fail_on to "{failOn}". Set it to "any" to fail on all of them.
validate.verdict_blocking: Result: the vault is conformant to the format, but findings above (guidance or house rules) block this run.
validate.verdict_broken: Result: the vault is not conformant to the format.
validate.verdict_unexpected: Result: at least one finding could not be classified; this run cannot say whether the vault is conformant. See the tool defect section above.
common.shape_unreadable: {field} is present but its shape could not be read (see PARSER_LIMITS in src/frontmatter.mjs)
common.timestamp_form: {field} "{value}" is not an ISO 8601 datetime with an explicit UTC offset, which section 5 requires for every timestamp-valued key
spec.type_required.unterminated: frontmatter opens with "---" but is never closed with a second one, so type cannot be confirmed; close the block
spec.type_required.no_frontmatter: type is required but missing (the file has no frontmatter at all)
spec.type_required.no_type_key: type is required but missing (this file has frontmatter, but no type key in it)
spec.type_required.empty: type is present but empty; it must be a non-empty string
spec.index_no_frontmatter.outside_root: index.md is reserved and must carry no frontmatter (only the root index may declare okf_version)
spec.index_no_frontmatter.extra_key: the root index may declare only okf_version and nothing else; found "{found}"
spec.log_format.has_frontmatter: log.md is reserved and should carry no frontmatter
spec.log_format.heading_calendar: log heading "## {heading}" is in YYYY-MM-DD form but names a day that does not exist; section 9 requires a real ISO 8601 date
spec.log_format.heading_form: log heading "## {heading}" is a date written in another form; section 9 requires date headings in ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD form
spec.log_format.heading_not_a_date: log heading "## {heading}" is not a date heading; a log groups its entries under dates
spec.log_format.ordering: log dates must run from most recent to oldest; "{date}" comes after "{previous}"
spec.generated_actor.missing_actor: generated.by is required but missing or empty
spec.verified_events.empty: verified is present but carries no events; remove the key or add at least one with by and at
spec.verified_events.missing_actor: verified[{index}].by is required but missing or empty
spec.verified_events.missing_timestamp: verified[{index}].at is required but missing or empty
spec.status_enum.invalid: status "{value}" is not one of draft, stable, deprecated
spec.stale_after_format.invalid: stale_after "{value}" must be an ISO 8601 datetime with an explicit UTC offset; section 5 requires this for every timestamp-valued key, so a plain date is no longer accepted here
spec.sources_resource.missing_resource: sources[{index}] is missing a non-empty resource
house.required_fields.missing: {key} is required by this vault's own configuration but is missing
house.required_fields.empty: {key} is required by this vault's own configuration but is empty
house.forbidden_fields.present: {key} is forbidden by this vault's own configuration but is present
house.type_enum.invalid: type "{value}" is not one of this vault's allowed types: {allowed}
house.extension_fields.boolean: {field} "{value}" must be a boolean (true or false)
house.extension_fields.date: {field} "{value}" must be an ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD)
house.extension_fields.enum: {field} "{value}" is not one of this vault's allowed values: {allowed}
house.link_style.file_relative: link {seen} starts with a slash, which resolves against the host, not the repository, and breaks where a human reviews the change; this vault requires file-relative links
house.link_style.bundle_absolute: link {seen} does not start with a slash; this vault requires bundle-absolute links
house.link_target_exists.broken: link target "{target}" does not resolve to anything in this vault (resolved to "{resolved}")
house.link_target_exists.unwalked: link target "{target}" exists on disk but is not part of what this command walked (resolved to "{resolved}"); it sits under validate.ignore_paths, a dot-entry or node_modules, so this run cannot vouch for it
house.no_wikilinks.forbidden: [[{target}]] is a wikilink, which this vault forbids; use a standard markdown link instead
house.root_okf_version.missing: the root index does not declare okf_version, which this vault requires
house.root_okf_version.mismatch: the root index declares okf_version "{value}" but this vault is configured for "{expected}"
lint.index_completeness.missing_index: the directory "{dir}" holds a markdown file but has no index.md
lint.index_completeness.dir_not_linked: the root index does not link the first-level directory "{dir}"
lint.orphans.unreachable: this note is not reachable by following links from the root index
lint.columns.missing_table: this file has no table to check against its configured column headings
lint.tables.missing_blank_line: this table has no blank line before its header row; this change touched the table, so the whole table was checked, not just the lines it added
lint.tables.missing_blank_line_full: this table has no blank line before its header row; this run checked the whole vault, so every table was checked, whether or not anything changed
lint.tables.duplicate_row: this data row duplicates the row at line {line}; this change touched the table, so the whole table was checked, not just the lines it added
lint.tables.duplicate_row_full: this data row duplicates the row at line {line}; this run checked the whole vault, so every table was checked, whether or not anything changed
lint.tables.cell_too_long: cell {index} has {length} characters, over the configured maximum of {max}; this change touched the table, so the whole table was checked, not just the lines it added
lint.tables.cell_too_long_full: cell {index} has {length} characters, over the configured maximum of {max}; this run checked the whole vault, so every table was checked, whether or not anything changed
lint.style.forbidden_char: this line was added by this change and uses the forbidden character "{char}"; style only judges lines a change added, not prose that was already in the vault
lint.style.forbidden_char_full: this line uses the forbidden character "{char}"; this run checked the whole vault, so every line was judged, not only lines a change added
lint.style.nothing_configured: the style rule is switched on for this vault but lint.style.forbidden_chars names no character, so this rule had nothing at all to look for; give it characters to forbid, or set lint.style to "off"
lint.secrets.pattern_matched_full: a line matches a secret-shaped pattern ({pattern}); never paste, print or share the matched text, rotate the credential now and follow the incident response steps in SECURITY.md
lint.secrets.truncated: this file carries more secret-shaped matches than could be listed: {shown} shown out of {total} found; treat every one as leaked, not only the ones named above, and follow SECURITY.md
lint.secrets.file_too_large: this file is {bytes} bytes, over the {max} byte limit for one file, so it was NOT scanned for secrets, and this run fails rather than calling it clean: nothing here was checked, which is not the same as nothing being here; if the file is known to be safe, list it under lint.secrets.exclude_paths, where the exclusion shows in review
lint.secrets.pattern_is_a_credential: an entry in privacy.secret_patterns is itself shaped like a real credential; that list is for DETECTION patterns, never for the secret you want detected, so rotate that credential now, remove it from the configuration and follow SECURITY.md
lint.privacy.linked_into_confidential: this file sits outside every confidential directory but links into one ("{target}"), exposing a confidential note from a place meant to be shared more broadly
lint.privacy.confidential_outside: this note carries confidential: true but sits outside every directory the configuration marks confidential
lint.attribution.missing_source_id: sources[{index}] has no id, so no footnote can ever anchor a claim to it
lint.attribution.unknown_footnote: this footnote key ("{key}") matches no id declared in sources; a footnote is meant to anchor a claim to one of the ids listed there
lint.attribution.source_not_anchored: sources declares the id "{id}" but no footnote in the body ever cites it; when a note draws on more than one source, this check expects each one to be anchored somewhere in the body
lint.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit lint: "{dir}" is not a directory.
lint.no_vault: brain-kit lint: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and {index}).
lint.unknown_base: brain-kit lint: unknown base "{base}" (expected one of: {ids}).
lint.unknown_rule: brain-kit lint: unknown rule "{rule}" (expected one of: {ids}).
lint.explain_error: These findings are treated as errors: this run fails because of them.
lint.explain_warn: These findings are warnings: they never fail this run.
lint.verdict_clean_but_partial: Result: no findings, but this run did not check everything (see the scope line above, and the skipped count below, if any); a clean report from a partial run is not the same as a clean vault.
lint.verdict_warnings_only: Result: only warnings above; this run does not fail because of them.
lint.verdict_failing: Result: this run fails because of the error(s) above.
lint.verdict_failing_too_large: Result: this run fails because of the error(s) above, {count} of them a file too large to scan for secrets, which was not read at all; that is not the same as clean.
lint.verdict_degraded: Result: this run is degraded ({causes}), so its results are incomplete; treat the findings above as partial, fix the cause named for each one, and rerun.
lint.degraded_part.timed_out: {count} file(s) took too long to scan for secrets and timed out
lint.degraded_part.scan_failed: {count} file(s) could not be scanned for secrets
lint.degraded_part.listing_failed: git could not list the files this vault would publish
lint.explain_defect: These are not findings about your vault: this tool itself failed to finish checking it. Every finding above them from a rule that did complete is still real; nothing above is.
lint.tool_defect.rule_crashed: the "{rule}" rule crashed and produced no results at all: {message}
lint.tool_defect.file_scan_failed: the secrets scan on this file failed and was abandoned rather than reported as complete: {message}
lint.tool_defect.file_scan_timed_out: the secrets scan on this file ran out of time and was abandoned rather than reported as complete: {message}
lint.tool_defect.file_read_failed: this file could not be read at all (error {code}), so it was not scanned for secrets
lint.tool_defect.file_name_undecodable: this file's name is not valid UTF-8, so it cannot be opened by name here and was not scanned for secrets; rename it
lint.tool_defect.publishable_list_failed: git could not list the files this vault would publish (git exited {status}), so the secrets rule read nothing at all; fix the repository and rerun
lint.scope.outside_repo: Scope: not inside a git repository, so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.scope.all_explicit: Scope: "all" was requested, so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.scope.no_commits: Scope: this repository has no commit yet, so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.scope.worktree_explicit: Scope: "worktree" was requested, checking what differs from HEAD.
lint.scope.merge_base_explicit: Scope: "merge-base" was requested, checking what changed since the merge base with "{defaultBranch}".
lint.scope.merge_base_unavailable: Scope: "merge-base" was requested, but no usable default branch or common ancestor was found, so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.scope.merge_base_same_as_current: Scope: "merge-base" was requested, but the default branch is the branch already checked out, so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.scope.auto_since_merge_base: Scope: "auto", checking everything committed since the merge base with "{defaultBranch}", plus the current worktree and any untracked file.
lint.scope.auto_merge_base_unavailable: Scope: "auto", but no usable merge base was found, checking what differs from HEAD, plus any untracked file.
lint.scope.auto_no_default_branch: Scope: "auto", but no default branch could be identified, checking what differs from HEAD, plus any untracked file.
lint.scope.auto_on_default_branch: Scope: "auto", already on the default branch, checking what differs from HEAD, plus any untracked file.
lint.scope.auto_on_default_branch_clean: Scope: "auto", already on the default branch with nothing left to compare against (a clean tree, nothing untracked), so every markdown note in the vault was checked, every line.
lint.secrets_reach_git: The secrets rule is never narrowed by the scope above: it read {count} file(s), every one git tracks or would add here, dot-files included, each as it stands in the working tree; files git ignores were not read, and neither is anything only a commit holds.
lint.secrets_reach_walk: The secrets rule is never narrowed by the scope above: this is not a git repository, so it read {count} file(s), every one the vault walk includes plus dot-files, except .git and anything under node_modules.
lint.scope_ignored_paths: Not checked at all, by this vault's own choice: validate.ignore_paths excludes {paths}, so nothing under those prefixes was read by any rule that ran.
lint.scope_ignored_paths_secrets_still_r: Not checked by the note rules, by this vault's own choice: validate.ignore_paths excludes {paths} from every rule but secrets, which still read every file git tracks or would add under them.
lint.secrets_excluded: Not scanned for secrets, by this vault's own choice: lint.secrets.exclude_paths excludes {paths}, {count} file(s) in all, and nothing under them was read by the secrets rule.
lint.secrets_exclude_unmatched: lint.secrets.exclude_paths names {paths}, which match no file this vault would publish, so they exclude nothing and those files were read: a path there is written relative to the vault root, the way git lists it, with no leading ./ or /.
lint.secrets_other_repositories: Not scanned for secrets: {paths}, each a submodule or a repository of its own, whose content is not in this repository.
lint.secrets_absent: Not scanned for secrets: {count} file(s) git tracks are missing from the working tree ({paths}), so what a commit holds for them was not read.
push_gate.usage: Usage: brain-kit push-gate <remote-name> <remote-url> --patterns personal|config (the pre-push reference lines on standard input)
push_gate.missing_remote: brain-kit push-gate: the remote name and the remote URL are required, in that order, as git hands them to a pre-push hook; refusing rather than guessing which remote this push goes to.
push_gate.missing_patterns: brain-kit push-gate: --patterns is required, naming the pattern list that judges this push ({expected}); there is no default, because a default is a list nobody chose.
push_gate.unknown_patterns: brain-kit push-gate: --patterns "{value}" is not a pattern list this gate knows (expected: {expected}); refusing rather than scanning with a list nobody chose.
push_gate.git_unrunnable: brain-kit push-gate: git could not be run ({reason}), so this gate cannot ask what the push contains; refusing to push.
push_gate.not_a_repository: brain-kit push-gate: the current directory is not inside a git repository, so there is no push here to enumerate; refusing rather than reading that as a push with nothing in it.
push_gate.enumeration_unrunnable: brain-kit push-gate: could not run the push enumeration, src/push/records.sh ({reason}); refusing to push without knowing what it carries.
push_gate.stream_too_large: brain-kit push-gate: the push enumeration listed more than {limit} bytes of records, more than this gate reads for one push; refusing rather than scanning part of it.
push_gate.enumeration_failed: brain-kit push-gate: the push enumeration exited {status}, so its list of what this push carries is not the whole push; refusing without scanning a partial list.
push_gate.enumeration_killed: brain-kit push-gate: the push enumeration was stopped by signal {signal} before it finished, so its list of what this push carries is not the whole push; refusing without scanning a partial list.
push_gate.git_killed: brain-kit push-gate: git was stopped by signal {signal} while this gate asked whether this is a repository, so it cannot say what the push contains; refusing to push.
push_gate.messages_too_large: brain-kit push-gate: the push enumeration wrote more than {limit} bytes of messages, more than this gate reads for one push; refusing without scanning.
push_gate.reference_count_mismatch: brain-kit push-gate: git sent {sent} reference line(s) for this push and the push enumeration listed {listed} reference(s), so some of what this push carries would go unscanned; refusing instead of calling it clean.
push_gate.reference_numbering: brain-kit push-gate: the push enumeration did not number its references 1 to {sent}, in the order git sent them, so its list does not describe this push; refusing instead of calling it clean.
push_gate.reference_name_mismatch: brain-kit push-gate: the destination name the push enumeration listed for reference #{number} of this push is not the one git sent on that line, so its list does not describe this push; refusing instead of calling it clean (neither name is printed).
push_gate.stdin_unreadable: brain-kit push-gate: the reference lines on standard input could not be read to the end ({reason}), so what did arrive is not the whole push; refusing instead of scanning part of it.
push_gate.not_a_vault: brain-kit push-gate: --patterns config reads this vault's {file}, and no vault was found from the current directory; refusing rather than scanning without the vault's patterns.
push_gate.config_unloadable: brain-kit push-gate: the working tree's {file} could not be loaded ({reason}), so this vault's patterns are unknown; refusing to push.
push_gate.config_outside_repository: brain-kit push-gate: this vault's {file} is outside the repository being pushed, so no default branch of it can hold one; this push is scanned with privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's copy alone.
push_gate.config_patterns_union: brain-kit push-gate: this push is scanned with the generic credential shapes and privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's {file}, from the configuration at {tips} pushed tip(s) and {carried} earlier commit(s) of this push, and from the default branch as this repository knows it ({branches}).
push_gate.default_branch_unresolved_name: brain-kit push-gate: no default branch of remote '{remote}' is known to this repository (none of its HEAD, main or master under refs/remotes/ resolves), so this push is scanned with privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's {file} and from the configurations this push carries alone. To add the default branch's, run: {command}
push_gate.default_branch_unresolved_by_u: brain-kit push-gate: '{remote}' is not the name of a remote, and no configured remote ({remotes}) has a default branch this repository knows (refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD, main or master), so this push is scanned with privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's {file} and from the configurations this push carries alone. To add them, run: git fetch --all
push_gate.default_branch_unresolved_no_r: brain-kit push-gate: '{remote}' is not the name of a remote and this repository has no remote configured, so no default branch is known and this push is scanned with privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's {file} and from the configurations this push carries alone. To add one, run: {command}
push_gate.default_branch_no_config: brain-kit push-gate: {branch}, a default branch as this repository knows it, has no {path}; it adds no patterns to this push.
push_gate.default_config_unusable: brain-kit push-gate: the {path} on {branch}, a default branch as this repository knows it, could not be used ({reason}); it adds no patterns to this push, which is scanned with the other sources.
push_gate.tip_config_unusable: brain-kit push-gate: the {path} at reference #{number} of this push could not be used ({reason}); it adds no patterns to this push, which is scanned with the other sources.
push_gate.default_branch_read_failed: brain-kit push-gate: could not read the {path} on {branch}, a default branch as this repository knows it ({reason}); refusing rather than scanning without the patterns a person merged there.
push_gate.tip_config_read_failed: brain-kit push-gate: could not read the {path} at reference #{number} of this push ({reason}); refusing rather than scanning without its patterns.
push_gate.pattern_uncompilable_working: brain-kit push-gate: a pattern in the working tree's {file} does not compile ({reason}); fix it there. Refusing to push.
push_gate.pattern_uncompilable_tip: brain-kit push-gate: a pattern in the {path} at reference #{number} of this push does not compile ({reason}); fix it in that commit. Refusing to push.
push_gate.pattern_uncompilable_default: brain-kit push-gate: a pattern in the {path} on {branch}, the default branch as this repository knows it, does not compile ({reason}). Every push is refused until it is fixed there, and a push that fixes it is refused too, so fix it through the host's own interface, then fetch. Refusing to push.
push_gate.default_branch_unresolved_unfe: brain-kit push-gate: this repository holds no remote-tracking branch of remote '{remote}', so this push is scanned with privacy.secret_patterns from the working tree's {file} and from the configurations this push carries alone. If nothing is published there yet, there is no merged configuration to add and nothing to run; if this clone has simply never fetched it, run: {command}
push_gate.carried_config_list_failed: brain-kit push-gate: could not list the commits of this push that change {path} ({reason}); refusing rather than scanning without their patterns.
push_gate.carried_config_read_failed: brain-kit push-gate: could not read the {path} at commit {commit} of this push ({reason}); refusing rather than scanning without its patterns.
push_gate.carried_config_unusable: brain-kit push-gate: the {path} at commit {commit} of this push could not be used ({reason}); it adds no patterns to this push, which is scanned with the other sources.
push_gate.pattern_uncompilable_carried: brain-kit push-gate: a pattern in the {path} at commit {commit} of this push does not compile ({reason}); fix it in that commit. Refusing to push.
